methods: Design: cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic. Population: Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination (analytic n = 6,701). Outcome: CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement). Exposure: Hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm Hg or antihypertensive use). Comparator: participants without the exposure, from the same survey population. Covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), Educational attainment, Smoking status, Body mass index. Descriptive: survey-weighted Table 1 by ckd - egfr <60 or uacr >=30 mg/g (single measurement); weighted prevalence with 95% CIs. Model: prevalence ratios (survey-weighted Poisson regression); sequential models: Unadjusted, Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity, Fully adjusted (primary). Effect modification: interaction tests and stratified estimates by sex, age group. Survey design: Taylor linearisation with strata and PSUs; weight WTMECPRP; design df = 25. Sensitivity analyses: 5 prespecified. Missing data: complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation as sensitivity. Reporting: STROBE; plan pre-registered by hash before data access.

limitations.text: Cross-sectional: exposure and outcome are measured at the same visit, so the direction of association cannot be established.
Residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded in an observational analysis.
Laboratory values come from a single blood or urine sample; transient abnormalities may be misclassified as persistent.
Complete-case loss: 18.2% of the analytic sample (1486) lack >=1 covariate. Multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis recommended.

Raw values within plausible ranges: Out-of-range values: BMXBMI (0 low, 1 high); BPXODI1 (0 low, 1 high); BPXOSY1 (1 low, 0 high); BPXOSY2 (2 low, 0 high); BPXOSY3 (2 low, 0 high); LBXGH (1 low, 0 high); URDACT (0 low, 2 high)

certainty.meaning: The true association may be substantially different from the estimate.

domains.reason: Cross-sectional design already reflected in the Low starting level; adjusted, pre-specified analysis with design audit passed.

US civilian non-institutionalised population; outcome measured directly.
95% CI 1.31-1.88 excludes no effect and is reasonably narrow.
Cannot be judged from a single study; pre-registration by plan hash reduces selective reporting.

rating_up.reason: No large effect or dose-response gradient.

certainty.caveat: GRADE rates bodies of evidence; this single-study rating summarises how much this analysis can contribute and should be re-rated in any systematic review.

assumptions: Outcome prevalence assumed 10% (run the blinded probe for the real rate band).
